Longitudinal (vertical) section of the mammalian heart in front view (so the right side of the heart is on the viewer's left). Show the four chambers with the thin-walled atria at the top and thick-walled ventricles below, the left ventricle wall clearly thickest, the septum, the tricuspid and bicuspid valves with chordae tendineae and papillary muscles, semilunar valves at the base of the pulmonary artery and aorta, and the major vessels. Blood on the right side tinted blue and on the left side tinted red, with small arrows showing flow.
